findings.evidence: p.119, §6.8: 'prefix caching is a partial mitigation (~13% of prefill FLOPs), not the fix for the 40 rps prefill queue'. The ~13% figure comes from p.117 (§6.3.4): 'the byte-identical share is at most the fixed system/instruction portion of the ~1,200-token prompt ... so ~13% of prefill FLOPs (the whole-slot case) is an upper bound on the cacheable fraction'. 1,200 ÷ 9,200 = 13.04%. The text calls it '~13%' on both pages. However, p.117 also says 'the 8K retrieved block differs per query and the 1,200-token slot carries the query itself (Ch 4 Table 4-1)', meaning the cacheable fraction could be LESS than 13% (the query part of the 1,200 tokens is not cacheable across queries). The '~13% (the whole-slot case)' phrasing acknowledges this but p.119 drops the '(the whole-slot case)' qualifier and the 'upper bound' language, presenting '~13% of prefill FLOPs' as a flat figure rather than an upper bound.
findings.issue: The '~13% of prefill FLOPs' figure loses its 'upper bound' and '(the whole-slot case)' qualifiers when restated on p.119 (§6.8). On p.117 it is explicitly an upper bound ('at most', 'upper bound on the cacheable fraction'); on p.119 it appears as a bare quantity ('~13% of prefill FLOPs'), which a reader could take as a measured or expected value rather than a ceiling.
findings.fix_instruction: On p.119, restore the qualifier: change '~13% of prefill FLOPs' to '~13% of prefill FLOPs (an upper bound; the cacheable fraction is smaller once the query tokens are excluded)' or simply '~≤13% of prefill FLOPs (upper bound, §6.3.4)'.

findings.evidence: "1. Workload metrics — what the system is being asked to do. Requests per second (rps) and the token profile (input length, output length, context length). These are the independent variables — the offered load; we do not control them, we characterize them. Admitted concurrency is a serving/scheduler state (Little's law), not a workload input. Fig 6.1's workload box lists concurrency alongside rps and the token profile: read that entry as offered concurrency — the arrival-side λ that the traffic offers — not as admitted or queued concurrency, which sits on the serving/scheduler side with queue depth."
findings.issue: Figure/body ontology contradiction (recurrence family: figure-vs-body classification conflicts). The body text now declares that Fig 6.1's workload box 'lists concurrency alongside rps and the token profile' and instructs the reader to reinterpret it as offered/arrival-side concurrency. The figure itself (rendered p. 129) shows the box labelled literally 'Workload metrics / rps · token profile · concurrency'. A figure that says 'concurrency' in a workload box, paired with a body sentence that must instruct the reader how NOT to read that box's own label, is a labelling defect: the figure's text contradicts the classification the prose admits it needs. The caption on p. 129 repeats the repair instruction ('Label caveat: the workload box's concurrency entry is offered concurrency (arrival-side), not admitted or queued concurrency') rather than fixing the figure, which means the taxonomy in the artifact is wrong and the prose is carrying an erratum. Same defect family as the queue-depth entry, which the figure places in a separate dashed band labelled 'scheduler state, not a serving metric' — concurrency receives no such treatment in the figure, only in prose.
findings.fix_instruction: Edit Fig 6.1 so the workload box reads 'rps · token profile · offered concurrency (λ)' (or move concurrency into a distinct arrival-side band parallel to the queue-depth band), so the figure's own text is not contradicted by the caption's caveat. Alternatively relabel the box to 'offered load: rps · token profile' and drop 'concurrency' from the figure entirely, keeping the arrival-side concurrency notion only in the body text. Then shorten the caption's 'Label caveat' sentence to a pointer rather than an erratum.

findings.evidence: Figure 6.1 in-figure text: 'Workload metrics / rps · token profile · concurrency', 'Resource metrics / HBM BW · MFU · KV occupancy · memory pressure', 'Serving metrics / TTFT · TPOT · goodput', and a separate band 'queue depth: scheduler state, not a serving metric'.
findings.issue: List-of-Figures / in-figure-heading divergence. The List of Figures (p. 10) describes Fig 6.1 as 'The metric hierarchy as a diagnostic chain [ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]'. The in-figure headings, however, are not neutral labels: the workload box says 'concurrency', while the body's §6.1.1 and the caption both insist concurrency is a serving/scheduler state and not a workload input. The figure therefore promotes a taxonomy error into an artifact that readers consult as a quick reference. This is a second, independent occurrence of the same defect family in a different form (the first being the caption's repair instruction), and it will recur wherever a figure in this book is used as a standalone reference card.
findings.fix_instruction: Regenerate Fig 6.1 with the three box headings matching the taxonomy exactly: 'Workload: rps · token profile · offered concurrency (λ)', 'Serving: TTFT · TPOT · goodput', 'Resource: HBM BW · MFU · KV occupancy · memory pressure', and keep queue depth in the scheduler-state band with an explicit 'scheduler state' label. Then verify the List of Figures entry (p. 10) still describes the figure accurately and that no other figure reuses the un-qualified term 'concurrency' in a workload box.

findings.evidence: "[DERIVED] (source keys: each [S#] names one entry in the References chapter, where [S3]–[S7] resolve; Ch 11 lists [S1]–[S6] inline.)"
findings.issue: Malformed / self-contradictory source-key pointer. The sentence states that '[S3]–[S7] resolve' and then immediately states 'Ch 11 lists [S1]–[S6] inline' — the two ranges overlap only partially ([S3]–[S6]) and the [S#] keyspace is not reconciled: if Ch 11 lists S1–S6 and Ch 6 uses S3–S7, then S7 appears in Ch 6 while the Ch 11 inline range stops at S6, leaving S7 without a stated home until the References chapter. The pointer form is also non-declared: the Preface's cross-reference conventions (p. 20) declare only '§ N.M', 'Ch N §M' and appendix 'A.N' forms; '[S#]' is an undocumented reference form. This is part of the malformed-cross-reference family: an undocumented pointer syntax used repeatedly across Chs 6, 11 and the References chapter.
findings.fix_instruction: Add '[S#]' to the Preface's declared cross-reference forms with the rule for its resolution (one entry in the References chapter), and reconcile the ranges: state explicitly which keys each chapter uses and which are shared (e.g. 'S1–S7 are book-wide; Ch 11 discusses S1–S6; S7 is introduced in Ch 6'). Fix the sentence so it no longer asserts two overlapping ranges without reconciliation.

findings.evidence: "Speculative decoding where decode bandwidth is the wall — DFlash reports over 6× lossless acceleration, up to 2.5× over EAGLE-3, in its paper's evaluated configurations [S5][1P][FACT] — because it reduces weight reads per accepted token. These are paper-reported results, not portable serving-speed figures: treat them as performance claims to re-measure on the target workload, not as a guaranteed speedup."
findings.issue: Label/provenance mismatch: the Preface (p. 17) defines [1P] as 'first-party: the model vendor's own spec', and the evidence boundary on p. 5 scopes [1P] to 'the model vendor's own spec'. A third-party research paper's own self-reported speedup is first-party relative to the paper but is not a 'model vendor's own spec' of the deployed model. The sentence itself concedes these are 'paper-reported results, not portable serving-speed figures' — i.e. the measurement status is PAPER-REPORTED / UNVALIDATED, not MEASURED, yet the tag pair given is [1P][FACT]. Same pattern at p. 135 ('Mooncake: a 525% throughput increase (simulated) and 75% more requests [S4][1P][FACT]') and p. 139 ('vLLM KV-offloading ... cuts TTFT by 2–22× in a particular warm-cache-hit/reuse benchmark ... [S7][1P][FACT]'), where a 'simulated' figure carries a [FACT] tag.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a provenance tag for 'first-party to a third-party research paper, as reported by its authors' (e.g. [PAPER]) or state in the Preface that [1P] means 'first-party to the cited source (vendor spec or paper's own reported result)' and extend Axis 3 with a status for 'as-reported-by-source, not independently reproduced'. Then re-tag the DFlash, Mooncake and vLLM-KV-offload figures accordingly, keeping the 'simulated' qualifier visible in the tag rather than only in prose.

findings.evidence: "Scenario A [ILLUSTRATIVE]: the extra 20 tok/s are produced, but they land in the tail that misses the SLO, so goodput does not grow. Raw throughput is up 40%; goodput (tokens that met the SLO) is effectively unchanged in this case, because the batch of SLO-compliant tokens didn't grow." — followed by "Scenario B [ILLUSTRATIVE]: if the compliant fraction falls from 96% to 94%, goodput is 50×0.96 = 48 vs 70×0.94 = 65.8 — it rises despite the p95 breach." and "Scenario C [ILLUSTRATIVE]: if the compliant fraction falls to 65% ... goodput is 70×0.65 = 45.5 tok/s — below the 48 tok/s baseline."
findings.issue: Illegal/ambiguous evidence label: an epistemic-status tag has been attached to a scenario label rather than to a claim. The Preface (p. 18) defines the Axis-2 vocabulary as 'FACT — directly stated by the source; DERIVED — computed by arithmetic from stated inputs; ASSUMPTION — a deliberately chosen scenario input, paired with a scenario provenance ([canonical scenario] or [ILLUSTRATIVE]); HYPOTHESIS — reasoned but not yet validated; UNRESOLVED'. 'Scenario A/B/C' is a scenario identifier, and '[ILLUSTRATIVE]' is an Axis-1 provenance tag; attaching it to a scenario name ('Scenario A [ILLUSTRATIVE]') rather than to the proposition makes the pair ambiguous — there is no Axis-2 element, so the 'label pair' rule on p. 18 ('a label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes') is violated three times in one paragraph block. The body then does supply the arithmetic (f ≈ 68.6%), but the Scenario A statement is asserted ('goodput does not grow') without a tag stating it is a DERIVED conclusion — and in fact Scenario A is only true if f = 68.6%, which the text says itself.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the three scenarios so each carries a proper pair, e.g. 'Scenario A [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]: at f = 68.6% (48 ÷ 70), goodput is unchanged at 48 tok/s', 'Scenario B [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]: at f = 94%, goodput = 65.8 tok/s', 'Scenario C [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]: at f = 65%, goodput = 45.5 tok/s'. Remove the bare '[ILLUSTRATIVE]' after the scenario names and add the missing 'DERIVED' that the arithmetic in the text performs.

findings.evidence: "The two-point approximation of the mean is E[L] ≈0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0 ≈0.84 s — looks fine. Three related numbers circulate in this paragraph, so we fix them once here, at first presentation: the two-point analytic mean is 0.842 s (0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0, written 0.84 s above); the plotted synthetic stream’s exact mean is 0.85 s (the value Fig 6.2 displays); and every percentile below is a property of the N = 10,000 sample, not of the distribution — the population p99 of this 99 % log-normal + 1 % straggler mixture is 5.0 s. Read off the sample, the long tail looks like this: p50 ≈ 0.80 s, p90 ≈ 0.94 s, p95 ≈ 0.99 s, and p99 ≈ 1.33 s — a knife-edge property of this N = 10,000 sample, not of the distribution: linear interpolation lands just past the largest non-straggler draw, between it and the first straggler (percentile position 1 + (N−1)×0.99 = 9,900.01; sorted-sample ranks: 9,900 → 1.30 s, 9,901 → 5.0 s; 1.30 + 0.01 × (5.0 − 1.30) ≈ 1.33 s), and the sample figure is knife-edge in the straggler count as well: with exactly 100 stragglers (1 % of 10,000) the interpolation above returns 1.33 s, while 101 of 10,000 puts a straggler at rank 9,900 itself, so both interpolation endpoints are 5.0 s draws and the sample p99 is 5.0 s."
findings.issue: ASD-STE100 readability defect: one sentence carries seven distinct qualifications, an interpolation formula, two rank positions and a conditional-counterfactual, and the paragraph re-states the same mean three times (0.84 / 0.842 / 0.85) with the parenthetical 'written 0.84 s above' pointing at a sentence the reader has just read. The 'knife-edge' reasoning (linear interpolation between rank 9,900 and 9,901) is a reproducibility note, not a body-text argument, and it is interleaved with the percentile claims it qualifies. The same sentence-level pattern recurs at p. 139 ('Three related numbers circulate…'), p. 111 and p. 145 — a recurring house style of embedding multi-clause reconciliation inside a single sentence. A reader chasing the headline (p99 ≈ 1.33 s vs population 5.0 s) must parse the whole apparatus before learning the point.
findings.fix_instruction: Split the paragraph: (1) state the four sample percentiles as a list; (2) state in one sentence that the sample p99 is knife-edge and why (one straggler changes it from 1.33 s to 5.0 s); (3) move the interpolation arithmetic (percentile position, rank values, the 1.30 + 0.01 × (5.0 − 1.30) computation) into a reproducibility note below the paragraph, consistent with the note style already used in the Fig 6.2 caption on p. 133. Remove the redundant restatement of 0.842 s.

findings.evidence: "TTFT 1.2 s / TPOT ~25 ms... p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s and p95 TPOT ≤ 35 ms"
findings.issue: Consistency check: Ch 4 Table 4-1 lists "TTFT budget 1.2 s ... TPOT budget ~25 ms/token; p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s, p95 TPOT ≤ 35 ms". Matches.
